questions.q: What does the VVKIK system begin with, according to the summary?
a: Vision and values
Income and savings
Goals and habits
Budget and tracking
questions.why: Lesson 1 says vision and values come first and act as mileposts for the rest of the system.

questions.q: What are income-generating tasks in the VVKIK system?
a: To-dos that bring the greatest return on your time
Chores you hand off to someone else
Weekly targets for your savings account
Skills you must learn before investing
questions.why: Lesson 1 says these tasks create the most wealth for the least time, so they deserve focus.

questions.q: How does the summary say to calculate your income-generating value?
a: Divide what you earn each week by the hours you work
Subtract your expenses from your monthly salary
Multiply your hourly wage by your years of experience
Add up the value of everything you own
questions.why: Lesson 2 gives the example of $1,000 a week over 55 hours, an hourly value of $18.

questions.q: What does the summary advise doing with work that pays less than your income-generating value?
a: Cut it out or pay someone else to do it
Do it first thing in the morning
Charge more for that same work
Save it for the weekend
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to drop low-value tasks or delegate them so your hourly value can rise.

questions.q: Why does the summary prefer a penny doubled daily for a month over a million dollars?
a: Compounding turns it into more than four million
It is safer than taking a lump sum
It teaches you to spend less each day
It grows at a steady linear rate
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses the thought experiment to show how quickly compounding outruns a large one-off sum.
